newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AGL signs deal to sell gas to Victoria.
newsitem.headline: AGL signs deal to sell gas to Victoria.

text.p: The Victoria state government said on Thursday the first agreement to sell gas sourced from South Australia's Cooper Basin into Victoria has been signed by Australian Gas Light Co and a Victorian gas distributor.

Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale said that under the agreement Australian Gas Light Co (AGL) would sell five petajoules (PJ) of gas a year for five years to Energy 21, one of three new gas retailers to be established by the Victorian government from July 1.

Stockdale said the agreement paved the way for the construction of a A$67 million gas pipeline to extend 146 km from Barnawartha, near Wadonga, on the Victoria-New South Wales border, to Wagga Wagga in New South Wales.
The pipeline will be built by East Australia Pipeline Ltd and the Victorian state-owned Gas Transmission Corp (GTC).
AGL owns 51 percent of East Australia Pipeline Ltd (EAPL) the remainder of the company is owned by foreign investors.

When completed the pipeline is expected to be able to carry 90 PJ a year in either direction between Victoria and New South Wales. "The agreement opens the way for the prospect of head to head gas competition for the first time, especially in northern Victoria," Stockdale said.

In a separate statement, AGL said the value of the contract was confidential. "We anticipate that once the EAPL and GTC systems are connected, we will see considerable trade in natural gas between the states," AGL managing director Len Bleasel said.
The EAPL/GTC pipeline is one of two proposed gas links between the two states in line with the opening up of competition in the gas industry.

The other is a 740 km east coast pipeline, taking Bass Strait gas from the Victorian plant of Longford to Sydney and Port Kembla which is being planned by the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd in partnership with Vancouver-based Westcoast Energy Inc.
